remediation.desc: Enable **Enhanced Monitoring** on RDS, using a `>0s` collection interval aligned to workload and cost. Assign a **least-privilege** role for log delivery, and apply **defense in depth** by centralizing logs, setting **alerts** on key OS metrics, and defining **retention** to support incident response and trend analysis.

risk_details:
Without **Enhanced Monitoring**, you lack **real-time OS telemetry**, delaying detection of resource saturation and abnormal activity.

This raises MTTR and risks **availability** impacts (timeouts, failovers), reduces **integrity** assurance during incidents, and weakens forensic visibility.

types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices

remediation.desc:
Create and maintain an **SNS-backed event subscription** for **DB parameter groups** that includes `configuration change` (or all) and keep it enabled.

- Apply **least privilege** to SNS topics
- Route to on-call/SIEM and test alerts
- Enforce change control and monitoring across all Regions

risk_details: Missing alerts on parameter changes erodes visibility. Attackers or mistakes can lower TLS requirements, disable auditing, or relax auth, enabling data exposure (**confidentiality**), unauthorized writes (**integrity**), or outages from unsafe settings (**availability**).

message: RDS security group event categories of configuration change and failure are not subscribed.
status_detail: RDS security group event categories of configuration change and failure are not subscribed.

analytic.name: RDS event subscription for DB security groups is enabled for configuration change and failure events

finding_info.desc: **RDS event subscriptions** are evaluated for **database security group** events. The check expects an enabled subscription with source type `db-security-group` that includes the `configuration change` and `failure` event categories.
finding_info.title: RDS event subscription for DB security groups is enabled for configuration change and failure events
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices

remediation.desc: Create or update an **RDS event subscription** for source type `db-security-group` including `configuration change` and `failure`. Route alerts to monitored channels, restrict topic access (**least privilege**), integrate with **incident response**, and enforce change control and **separation of duties** for security group updates.

risk_details: Missing alerts on **security group changes** or **failures** reduces visibility and slows response. Undetected rule changes can expose databases, while unnoticed failures prolong outages, impacting **confidentiality** and **availability** through unauthorized access or service disruption.

remediation.desc: Upgrade enrolled DB instances to an engine version covered under standard support to stop Extended Support charges. For new DB instances and restores created via automation, explicitly set the engine lifecycle support option to avoid unintended enrollment in RDS Extended Support when that is your policy.

risk_details: DB instances enrolled in RDS Extended Support can incur additional charges after the end of standard support for the running database major version. Remaining on older major versions can also delay necessary upgrades, increasing operational and security risk.

remediation.desc:
Enable **IAM database authentication** for supported engines and apply **least privilege** with scoped IAM policies. Prefer **short-lived tokens** over static DB passwords, enforce TLS, and phase out embedded credentials.

Monitor authentication activity with audit logs for **defense in depth**.

risk_details:
Absent **IAM-based, short-lived tokens**, databases rely on **static passwords** in code and configs, increasing theft and reuse.

Compromised DB creds enable unauthorized queries, leading to **data exfiltration** and tampering, and weaken **centralized access control** and rotation.

remediation.desc: Deploy all RDS instances in a **VPC**, preferably in **private subnets**. Enforce **least privilege** with security groups, network ACLs, and restrictive routing. Use private connectivity (peering, VPN, Direct Connect), avoid public exposure, and apply **defense in depth** through segmentation and monitoring.

risk_details: Without VPC isolation, databases may expose internet-reachable endpoints and lack granular network controls. This degrades **confidentiality** and **availability** via scanning/brute force and data exfiltration, and threatens **integrity** through unauthorized connections and lateral movement.

Enforce **least privilege** on log access, set retention, and define metrics/alarms for critical patterns. Integrate with a SIEM. risk_details: Without centralized RDS logs, database activity lacks visibility, hindering detection and response. Credential misuse, SQL injection, data exfiltration, and privilege abuse may go unnoticed, risking **confidentiality** and **integrity**. Unseen errors and slow queries can lead to outages, impacting **availability**.

remediation.desc: Enable `auto_minor_version_upgrade` on RDS instances so minor releases are applied promptly. Use maintenance windows and stage testing to limit impact. Follow **defense in depth** and **least privilege**; keep reliable backups and Multi-AZ to preserve continuity if upgrades require rollback.

risk_details: Without automatic minor upgrades, databases miss **security patches**, leaving known vulnerabilities exploitable and risking **unauthorized data access**. Unapplied fixes can cause **data corruption** and outages, harming **integrity** and **availability**.

message: RDS Instance securenotes-demo-db does not have multi-AZ enabled.

remediation.desc: Apply fault-tolerance and redundancy principles: enable **Multi-AZ** for production RDS workloads. Choose one standby or two readable standbys based on RTO/RPO and performance needs. Regularly test failover, monitor configuration drift, and allow exceptions only with documented, risk-based approval.

risk_details: Without **Multi-AZ**, an Availability Zone or instance failure can cause extended downtime and rely on restores, risking loss of recent writes. This degrades **availability** and may affect **integrity**, interrupting applications and breaching SLAs.

remediation.desc:
Keep databases private by applying **least privilege** at the network layer:
- Set `PubliclyAccessible` to `false`
- Place instances in private subnets
- Deny `0.0.0.0/0` and `::/0` on the DB port
- Expose access via private endpoints, VPN, or an application tier/DB proxy

Adopt **defense in depth** with monitoring and strong auth.

risk_details:
An internet-reachable database invites:
- Brute-force and vulnerability probing, risking **availability** and **integrity**
- Unauthorized queries and dumps leading to **confidentiality** loss

Compromise can enable **lateral movement** and persistence within the VPC.

remediation.desc:
Use a **non-default DB port** and enforce **defense in depth**:
- Apply **least-privilege** network rules
- Keep databases in **private subnets**; avoid public exposure
- Require strong authentication and audit logging

*Update client connection strings and security rules when the port changes.*

risk_details: Using a **default DB port** increases exposure to broad scans and eases **service fingerprinting**. With weak network controls, attackers can run **credential brute force**, target known **engine exploits**, or trigger **DoS** on the predictable port, threatening confidentiality and availability.

remediation.desc: Assign all non-Aurora RDS to an **AWS Backup plan** aligned to business `RPO/RTO`. Use **tags** for automatic coverage, define retention and lifecycle, and store backups in **immutable** vaults where possible. Regularly perform restore tests. Enforce **least privilege** and **separation of duties** for backup administration.

risk_details: Without an **AWS Backup plan**, databases lack assured recovery, degrading **availability** and **integrity**. Likely outcomes: accidental deletion, corruption, or malicious wipes with no recent restore point. Expect missed `RPO/RTO`, extended outages, and data inconsistency after incidents.

remediation.desc: Enable **encryption at rest** for all RDS instances. Prefer **customer-managed KMS keys** to control rotation and fine-grained access, applying **least privilege** and **defense in depth**. Restrict key usage, monitor key activity, and manage key lifecycle. Migrate unencrypted instances via encrypted snapshot copy and restore.

risk_details: Without **encryption at rest**, database files, snapshots, and automated backups remain in plaintext. An attacker with access to copied snapshots, compromised backups, or underlying storage can read sensitive data, causing loss of **confidentiality** and enabling large-scale exfiltration.

message: RDS Instance securenotes-demo-db connections use SSL encryption.
status_detail: RDS Instance securenotes-demo-db connections use SSL encryption.

analytic.name: RDS instance or cluster enforces SSL/TLS encryption for client connections

finding_info.desc: **RDS DB instances** and **DB clusters** enforce **SSL/TLS** for client connections via parameter groups. The check looks for `rds.force_ssl=1` (PostgreSQL, SQL Server) or `require_secure_transport` enabled (MySQL-family) and identifies databases where encryption enforcement isn't active.

remediation.desc:
Enforce transport encryption at the database layer:
- Enable `rds.force_ssl=1` or `require_secure_transport` in parameter groups
- Configure clients to require certificate validation and prevent fallback
- Use current TLS versions and trusted CAs
- Prefer private network access as **defense in depth**

risk_details: Without enforced **TLS**, clients can connect or downgrade to plaintext, exposing credentials and queries to interception. Adversaries can perform **MITM**, steal secrets, and tamper traffic, undermining **confidentiality** and **integrity** and enabling reuse of captured database credentials.

message: RDS Instance Snapshot rds:securenotes-demo-db-2026-11-02-21-05 is encrypted.
status_detail: RDS Instance Snapshot rds:securenotes-demo-db-2026-11-02-21-05 is encrypted.

analytic.name: RDS DB instance snapshot or DB cluster snapshot is encrypted

finding_info.desc: **RDS DB snapshots** and **DB cluster snapshots** are evaluated for **encryption at rest**, identifying snapshots created with a KMS key versus unencrypted ones.
finding_info.title: RDS DB instance snapshot or DB cluster snapshot is encrypted
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc: Encrypt all RDS snapshots at rest using **KMS**, preferably **customer-managed keys**. Apply **least privilege** to key usage, enforce encryption via templates and automation, and prevent sharing of unencrypted backups. Use **key rotation**, separation of duties, and ensure copies and cross-account shares remain encrypted.

risk_details: Unencrypted snapshots enable direct access to full database data if backups are leaked, cross-account shared, or stolen. Adversaries can harvest data offline, bypassing network controls, leading to **loss of confidentiality**. Restores from such snapshots propagate the exposure to new instances.

message: RDS Instance Snapshot rds:securenotes-demo-db-2026-11-02-21-05 is not shared.
status_detail: RDS Instance Snapshot rds:securenotes-demo-db-2026-11-02-21-05 is not shared.

analytic.name: RDS snapshot is not publicly shared

finding_info.desc:
**RDS DB snapshots** and **DB cluster snapshots** with **public visibility** (shared with `all` AWS accounts) are detected.

Snapshots limited to specific accounts or kept private are identified as restricted.
finding_info.title: RDS snapshot is not publicly shared
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Effects/Data Exposure
TTPs/Collection

remediation.desc:
Keep **RDS snapshots** and **cluster snapshots** private. Share only with explicit AWS account IDs using **least privilege** and time-bound access.

Enforce guardrails to block `public` visibility, require approvals for sharing, and audit snapshot permissions. Use encryption with strict key policies to control who can restore data.

risk_details:
Public RDS snapshots expose full database copies to all AWS accounts, risking:
- Loss of confidentiality via data exfiltration (PII, secrets)
- Offline cracking of hashes and schema reconnaissance
- Credential harvesting from dumps enabling lateral movement
This directly compromises confidentiality and fuels targeted attacks.

message: Resource Explorer Indexes found: 2.
status_detail: Resource Explorer Indexes found: 2.

analytic.name: Resource Explorer indexes exist

finding_info.desc: **AWS Resource Explorer** has user-owned **indexes** present in the account. The assessment determines whether at least one index exists in any enabled Region for resource cataloging and search.
finding_info.title: Resource Explorer indexes exist
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices

remediation.desc: Create **Resource Explorer indexes** in all active Regions and designate an **aggregator index** for cross-Region search. Apply least-privilege access to views, align with tagging standards, and routinely verify indexing status. This improves inventory accuracy, supports defense-in-depth, and speeds detection and remediation.

risk_details: Absent indexes reduce asset visibility, creating blind spots where misconfigured or orphaned resources go unnoticed. This degrades **confidentiality** (unseen public exposure), **integrity** (unauthorized changes undetected), and **availability** (slower containment and recovery), prolonging incident response and enabling lateral movement.

status_detail: Block Public Access is configured for the account 264350941467.

analytic.name: S3 account-level Block Public Access ignores public ACLs and restricts public buckets

finding_info.desc: **Amazon S3** account-level **Block Public Access** is assessed for `ignore_public_acls` and `restrict_public_buckets` to confirm centralized blocking of ACL-based public access and limiting buckets with public policies to in-account principals.
finding_info.title: S3 account-level Block Public Access ignores public ACLs and restricts public buckets
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc: Turn on account-level **Block Public Access** (prefer enabling all four: `block_public_acls`, `ignore_public_acls`, `block_public_policy`, `restrict_public_buckets`) to enforce least privilege. For legitimate access, use private buckets with **CloudFront**, VPC endpoints, or presigned URLs. Regularly review policies with IAM Access Analyzer.

risk_details:
Absent these settings, **public ACLs** and broad bucket policies may grant internet or cross-account access. This risks:
- Confidentiality: bulk data exfiltration
- Integrity: object overwrite/tampering
- Availability: malicious deletions or malware hosting, triggering takedowns

message: S3 Bucket securenotes-cloudtrail-264350941467 has bucket ACLs disabled.
status_detail: S3 Bucket securenotes-cloudtrail-264350941467 has bucket ACLs disabled.

analytic.name: S3 bucket has bucket ACLs disabled

finding_info.desc: **Amazon S3 buckets** are evaluated for **Object Ownership** set to `BucketOwnerEnforced`, which disables bucket and object ACLs. Buckets using any other ownership setting indicate that ACLs remain enabled.
finding_info.title: S3 bucket has bucket ACLs disabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark

remediation.desc: Disable ACLs by setting **Object Ownership** to `BucketOwnerEnforced` and manage access with **IAM** and **bucket policies** under **least privilege**. Centralize authorization, review policies regularly, and use organizational guardrails to prevent re-enabling ACLs. *Migrate ACL-based grants into policies before the change.*

risk_details:
With **ACLs enabled**, access can bypass centralized policy controls, impacting confidentiality and integrity.
- Unintended public or cross-account reads/writes
- Object-writer ownership blocking bucket-owner governance
- Per-object grants hinder auditing, enabling data exfiltration or tampering

message: S3 Bucket securenotes-cloudtrail-264350941467 has a bucket policy but it does not allow cross account access.
status_detail: S3 Bucket securenotes-cloudtrail-264350941467 has a bucket policy but it does not allow cross account access.

unmapped.notes: This check supports the `trusted_account_ids` configuration in config.yaml to allow specific cross-account access without triggering a finding.

analytic.name: S3 bucket policy does not allow cross-account access

finding_info.desc:
**Amazon S3 bucket policies** are analyzed for statements that grant **cross-account access**.

Any policy that names principals outside the owning account (other account IDs or `Principal: "*"`) is treated as cross-account; absence of a policy implies no cross-account grants.
finding_info.title: S3 bucket policy does not allow cross-account access
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
TTPs/Initial Access/Unauthorized Access
Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc:
Enforce **least privilege**: limit bucket policy `Principal` to your account or approved org IDs with fixed values; avoid wildcards.

Use **role-based cross-account access** with scoped permissions when needed. Add **defense-in-depth** conditions (private networks, TLS), and periodically review for unintended external access.

risk_details:
Cross-account grants can let external principals read, write, or administer the bucket, impacting:
- Confidentiality: unauthorized object access/exfiltration
- Integrity: object tampering, policy or encryption changes
- Availability: deletions, versioning changes, or lockouts causing data loss and downtime

message: S3 Bucket securenotes-cloudtrail-264350941467 does not have correct cross region replication configuration.
status_detail: S3 Bucket securenotes-cloudtrail-264350941467 does not have correct cross region replication configuration.

analytic.name: S3 bucket has cross-region replication configured to a bucket in a different region

finding_info.desc:
**Amazon S3 buckets** use **cross-Region replication** with `versioning` and an enabled rule that targets a destination bucket in a different AWS Region.

Buckets with same-Region targets, missing destinations, or disabled `versioning` don't meet this replication posture.
finding_info.title: S3 bucket has cross-region replication configured to a bucket in a different region
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Effects/Data Destruction

remediation.desc:
Enable **CRR** to a different Region with `versioning` and least-privilege roles.

- Replicate needed prefixes and metadata
- Consider `S3 Replication Time Control` for tighter RPO
- Protect deletes via `delete marker` strategy and Object Lock
- Monitor replication metrics and test DR regularly

Align with **defense in depth** and availability by design.

risk_details:
**Single-Region storage** creates an availability gap: a Regional outage, control-plane isolation, or denial of service can make data **unreachable**.

Lack of replication raises RPO/RTO, delaying recovery and disrupting multi-Region workloads. Missing replicas also weaken data **integrity** during restore from corruption or deletion.

analytic.name: [DEPRECATED] S3 bucket has default server-side encryption (SSE) enabled

finding_info.desc: [DEPRECATED] **Amazon S3 buckets** have a default **server-side encryption** setting that automatically encrypts new objects using `SSE-S3` or `SSE-KMS`. This evaluates whether a bucket has a default encryption configuration defined.

remediation.desc: Enable default encryption on all buckets, preferring `SSE-KMS` for sensitive data to retain key control and auditing. message: S3 Bucket securenotes-cloudtrail-264350941467 does not have event notifications enabled.
status_detail: S3 Bucket securenotes-cloudtrail-264350941467 does not have event notifications enabled.

analytic.name: S3 bucket has event notifications enabled

finding_info.desc: **Amazon S3 buckets** define a **notification configuration** that publishes bucket events (for example `s3:ObjectCreated:*`, `s3:ObjectRemoved:*`) to a destination. The evaluation identifies buckets that lack any notification setup.
finding_info.title: S3 bucket has event notifications enabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/NIST 800-53 Controls

remediation.desc:
Enable **S3 event notifications** for relevant events (e.g., `s3:ObjectCreated:*`, `s3:ObjectRemoved:*`) and route to controlled destinations (SNS, SQS, Lambda, EventBridge).

Use prefix/suffix filters, avoid recursive triggers, and enforce **least privilege** on targets. Pair with object-level logging for **defense in depth**.

risk_details: Missing notifications leaves object and bucket changes **unseen**, weakening **integrity** and **availability** oversight. Undetected deletions, policy drift, or replication issues can stall data pipelines (S3 to Lambda/SQS), slow incident response, and allow tampering or exfiltration to persist longer.

analytic.name: S3 bucket has server-side encryption with AWS KMS

finding_info.desc: **Amazon S3 buckets** use server-side encryption with **AWS KMS** keys, including dual-layer `aws:kms:dsse`. The evaluation identifies buckets whose default encryption is `aws:kms` or `aws:kms:dsse` rather than SSE-S3.
finding_info.title: S3 bucket has server-side encryption with AWS KMS
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc: Enable default **SSE-KMS** (or **DSSE-KMS** for highly sensitive data). Use a customer-managed key, enforce **least privilege** and separation of duties for key usage, and require KMS encryption via bucket policy (specify `aws:kms` and a designated key). Monitor key activity in **CloudTrail** and consider **S3 Bucket Keys** to control cost.

risk_details: Without **KMS-based encryption**, data relies only on SSE-S3, reducing **confidentiality** controls. Missing key policies and grants weakens **least privilege**, cross-account scoping, and the ability to disable or rotate keys. Lack of **KMS audit trails** obscures key usage, hindering detection of misuse and **defense in depth**.

finding_info.desc:
**Amazon S3 buckets** are evaluated for **Block Public Access** settings, ensuring `ignore_public_acls` and `restrict_public_buckets` are enabled at the bucket or account scope.

types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability

Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc: Enable **Block Public Access** at account and bucket levels with `block_public_acls`, `ignore_public_acls`, `block_public_policy`, and `restrict_public_buckets` set to `true`. message: S3 Bucket securenotes-cloudtrail-264350941467 has a lifecycle configuration enabled.
status_detail: S3 Bucket securenotes-cloudtrail-264350941467 has a lifecycle configuration enabled.

analytic.name: S3 bucket has a lifecycle configuration enabled

finding_info.desc: **Amazon S3 buckets** use **Lifecycle configurations** with at least one rule `Status: Enabled` to automate object `Transitions` and `Expiration` based on age, prefix, or tags
finding_info.title: S3 bucket has a lifecycle configuration enabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices

remediation.desc: Define **Lifecycle policies** by data classification: set `Expiration` to enforce retention, use `Transitions` to lower-cost classes, and enable `AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload`. For critical logs, keep versioning and, *if required*, **Object Lock**. Limit who can change lifecycle using least privilege and separation of duties.

risk_details: Without lifecycle rules, objects persist indefinitely, driving costs and retaining sensitive data beyond policy. Unchecked log/version growth strains operations and recovery. Long-lived data increases exposure if the account is compromised and can break required deletion timelines, affecting confidentiality and availability.

remediation.desc: Enable **MFA Delete** on sensitive, versioned buckets so permanent deletions and `Versioning` changes require a second factor. risk_details:

This erases recovery points, degrading data **availability**, weakening **integrity**, and increasing the blast radius of account compromise or ransomware.

finding_info.title: S3 bucket has Object Lock enabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Effects/Data Destruction

remediation.desc:
Enable **Object Lock** for critical data and set appropriate default retention in `GOVERNANCE` or `COMPLIANCE` mode.

Apply **immutability** and **least privilege** by restricting permissions that bypass retention, and use legal holds when you need indefinite protection for investigations or regulatory requirements.

risk_details:

Threats include ransomware erasing backups, insider or mistaken deletions, and tampering that defeats recovery. Inability to enforce retention or legal holds increases exposure to data loss and compliance gaps.

remediation.desc: Attach the **AWS Core rule set** to every Web ACL and add the managed rule groups that match the protected stack (PHP, SQL database, known bad inputs). Keep the default rule group version so vendor updates apply automatically, and review sampled requests before moving rules from Count to Block.

risk_details: A Web ACL built only from custom rules receives no vendor-maintained signatures, so newly disclosed exploitation patterns against the protected application reach the backend uninspected until someone writes a rule by hand. Managed rule groups are the compensating control cloud providers ship while runtime patches roll out, including request body size limits and runtime-specific rules.

remediation.desc: Enable **CloudWatch metrics** for all WAF rules and rule groups (*including managed rule groups*). Use consistent metric names, centralize dashboards and alerts, and review trends to validate rule efficacy. Integrate with a SIEM for **defense in depth** and tune rules based on telemetry.

risk_details: Absent **CloudWatch metrics**, WAF telemetry is lost, masking spikes, rule bypasses, and misconfigurations. This delays detection of SQLi/XSS probes and bot floods, risking data confidentiality, request integrity, and application availability.

remediation.desc: Populate each web ACL with targeted rules or managed rule groups to enforce least-privilege web access: cover common exploits (SQLi/XSS), IP reputation, and rate limits, scoped to your apps. Use a conservative `DefaultAction`, monitor metrics/logs, and continually tune-supporting **defense in depth** and **zero trust**.

risk_details: Without rules, traffic is governed only by the web ACL `DefaultAction`, often allowing requests without inspection. This increases risks to **confidentiality** (data exfiltration via injection), **integrity** (XSS/parameter tampering), and **availability** (layer-7 DDoS, bot abuse).
